note: Illustrative numbers: the shoppers, conversion rates, booking values, complaint rates and test effects are invented assumptions and don't describe any airline.

seat.label: Preselected seat
seat.desc: Should a paid seat be ticked by default? Shoppers can untick it, but many won't notice. Revenue usually rises, and so do refund requests.

a.title: No seat chosen
a.detail: Shoppers pick a seat or skip; skippers get a free seat at check-in.

b.title: Standard seat ticked, $18
b.detail: A standard seat is preselected on the extras page. Shoppers can untick it.

seat.legal: In the EU, optional extras must be opt-in (Regulation (EC) No 1008/2008, Art. 23), so this variant could only be tested elsewhere.

bundle.label: Bundle contents
bundle.desc: Does adding priority boarding to the comfort pack, for $4 more, earn more per shopper? A small change in a small share of bookings: hard to detect.

a.title: Comfort pack, $55
a.detail: Standard seat and one checked bag, offered after the fare is chosen.

b.title: Comfort pack plus, $59
b.detail: The same seat and bag, plus priority boarding.

price.label: Bag price point
price.desc: Raise the checked-bag price bought during booking from $35 to $40. More revenue per bag, fewer bags, and a few shoppers who give up.

a.title: Checked bag $35
a.detail: Price for the first checked bag when added during booking.

order.label: Display order
order.desc: Show the fare families with Standard first and labelled "Most chosen" instead of cheapest first. Shoppers trade up, or some leave.

a.title: Basic, Standard, Flex
a.detail: Fare families listed cheapest first, no label.

b.title: Standard first, "Most chosen"
b.detail: Standard leads the list with a label; Basic and Flex follow.
